title: Emit structured audit events for KMS operations and wire to audit logging pipeline
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes: Security: KMS operations now emit structured audit events (key usage + failures) into the audit pipeline.
Ops: New audit event types enable evidence collection for rotation and KMS failure-mode testing.
description: Summary: This PR emits structured audit events for KMS operations (encrypt/decrypt key usage + failure conditions) and forwards them through the existing audit logging pipeline. Motivation: Enterprise customers and GRC require evidence for key lifecycle/usage and we need consistent signals for KMS-related incidents (AccessDenied, disabled keys, throttling/timeouts) without leaking sensitive material. This change also supports the KMS hardening project by providing a stable schema for game days and post-incident review. Scope: (1) Define event types + schema for kms.encrypt, kms.decrypt, kms.decrypt_failed, kms.encrypt_failed, kms.policy_denied, kms.key_disabled (and provider-specific variants) (2) Emit events from the shared KMS client wrapper used by data-plane encryption paths (3) Dedupe/suppress high-volume success events with a bounded in-memory window (key_id+op+tenant) while always emitting failures (4) Wire events into audit-ingest with correct routing/tenancy and retention tags (5) Add unit/integration tests and documentation comments for schema stability. Non-goals: No change to cryptographic primitives; no plaintext/payload logging; no new external dependencies. Safety/Privacy: Events intentionally exclude plaintext, ciphertext, DEKs, request bodies, prompts, and model outputs. Key identifiers are recorded as provider key resource identifiers (e.g., AWS key ARN) and key version when available; we do not record raw IAM principals beyond the service identity and policy outcome. Dedupe behavior: Successful encrypt/decrypt events are emitted at most once per (tenant_id, deployment_mode, provider, key_id, op) per 10 minutes per process; failures are always emitted. Rollout: Gated behind audit.kms_events.enabled (default off) and audit.kms_events.success_dedupe_window=10m. On by default in staging; canary enable for Dedicated/Private first per ENG-4217 rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Schema reviewed with GRC (control mapping + retention tags) - [x] No secrets/PII logged (lint rule + tests) - [x] Unit tests for emitted fields and error mapping - [x] Integration test verifying audit-ingest acceptance - [x] Docs comments + examples for incident response - [x] Feature flag + safe defaults. References: Confluence spec: security-and-compliance/audit-logging/kms-key-lifecycle-audit-events (draft); Related: ENG-4234 (failure-mode harness) and PR 28741 (retry/backoff/circuit breaker).

kms: emit audit events for encrypt/decrypt success + failures
audit-ingest: route kms.* events with tenant + deployment tags

notable_snippet: New event types (packages/audit-schema/src/events/kms.ts): export type KmsAuditEvent = { event_type: 'kms.encrypt' | 'kms.decrypt' | 'kms.encrypt_failed' | 'kms.decrypt_failed' | 'kms.policy_denied' | 'kms.key_disabled'; occurred_at: string; tenant_id: string; deployment_mode: 'hosted' | 'dedicated' | 'private'; provider: 'aws_kms' | 'gcp_kms' | 'azure_key_vault'; key_id: string; key_version?: string; region?: string; component: 'data-plane' | 'control-plane' | 'installer'; operation_id: string; latency_ms?: number; outcome: 'success' | 'failure'; error_code?: string; error_detail_sanitized?: string; request_id?: string; deduped?: boolean; }; Emission site (services/crypto-kms/src/client/kms_client.ts): emitAuditEvent({ event_type: 'kms.decrypt_failed', outcome: 'failure', error_code: mapped.code, error_detail_sanitized: mapped.sanitizedMessage, key_id: ctx.keyId, key_version: ctx.keyVersion, tenant_id: ctx.tenantId, deployment_mode: ctx.deploymentMode, provider: ctx.provider, operation_id: ctx.opId, latency_ms: timer.ms(), request_id: providerRequestId });
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security) 2025-02-19: Please confirm we never emit raw AccessDenied messages from providers; those often include principal ARNs and policy statements. Also want explicit mapping for DisabledException vs NotFound vs Throttling so game day can assert behaviors. Kevin Osei 2025-02-19: Good call. I added error_mapping.ts that normalizes provider errors into a small enum + sanitized message (drops principal/policy strings, only keeps high-level reason). Added test coverage for AccessDenied redaction. Olga Petrov (GRC) 2025-02-20: For evidence, we need immutable event_type names and stable fields across versions. Can we mark key_version as optional but consistent (null vs omitted)? Also add retention tag classification so audit pipeline applies enterprise retention. Kevin Osei 2025-02-20: Updated schema to omit absent optional fields (no nulls) and added validator that enforces required fields for each event_type. Added routing tag audit_category='security' and control_tags=['KMS_USAGE','KMS_FAILURE'] in audit-ingest. Allison Grant (Observability) 2025-02-21: Emitting success events on every decrypt will be extremely high volume. The dedupe window needs to be configurable and we should expose counters for emitted vs deduped. Kevin Osei 2025-02-21: Implemented per-process LRU with TTL (default 10m) and added metrics: kms_audit_events_emitted_total{event_type,outcome} and kms_audit_events_deduped_total{event_type}. Sean Gallagher (SRE) 2025-02-22: In incidents we need correlation between audit events and request traces. Can we include operation_id that matches the request context trace id? Kevin Osei 2025-02-22: Wired operation_id to the existing request context correlation id (falls back to generated UUID if absent). Added integration test asserting audit event carries the same op id as the request context in the test harness. Jordan Lee (Policy) 2025-02-23: For policy denies, can we distinguish service IAM deny vs customer key policy deny (Private)? That distinction matters for runbooks. Kevin Osei 2025-02-23: Added error_code mapping to include POLICY_DENIED_SERVICE vs POLICY_DENIED_KEY_POLICY when provider gives enough signal; otherwise POLICY_DENIED_UNKNOWN. Added note in code comments + tests for AWS KMS AccessDeniedException variants. Marcus Lin 2025-02-24: Approved. Please ensure flag default remains off in prod until we validate volume in staging. Kevin Osei 2025-02-24: Confirmed: audit.kms_events.enabled defaults to false and is set in staging config only. Merging.
